metadata.representation: IF-THEN production rules with Certainty Factors (CF) ∈ [-1, +1]

rules.explanation: ADA criterion: HbA1c ≥ 6.5% in an adult ≥30 yr is diagnostic of T2DM.
Two abnormal glucose readings (FPG ≥126 and 2-h PP ≥200) confirm diabetes (ADA).
Random glucose ≥200 mg/dL plus classic hyperglycaemic symptoms is diagnostic (ADA).
Young patient (<30) with hyperglycaemia and unintentional weight loss suggests T1DM.
Adult-onset diabetes in a non-obese patient with weight loss is suggestive of LADA.
HbA1c 5.7-6.4%, FPG 100-125 or 2-h PP 140-199 fall in the prediabetes range (ADA).
Elevated TSH with fatigue strongly suggests primary hypothyroidism.
Suppressed TSH with weight loss is consistent with hyperthyroidism.
BMI ≥30 is an established risk factor for T2DM.
HTN doubles cardiovascular risk in diabetics.
HbA1c ≥9% indicates poor glycaemic control with high risk of micro/macrovascular complications.
Tingling/numbness in a diabetic patient is highly suggestive of peripheral neuropathy.
Blurred vision in a diabetic warrants a dilated-eye examination.
Elevated serum creatinine in a diabetic suggests evolving nephropathy.
Delayed wound healing plus diabetes raises diabetic-foot risk; perform foot exam.

then.value: First-line: lifestyle modification + Metformin 500-1000 mg BID

rules.explanation: ADA: Metformin is first-line in T2DM with HbA1c <7.5%.

then.value: Dual therapy: Metformin + (SGLT2-i / GLP-1 RA / DPP4-i)

rules.explanation: Moderate hyperglycaemia warrants dual oral therapy (ADA Section 9).

then.value: Initiate basal insulin ± oral agents and refer to endocrinology

rules.explanation: Severe hyperglycaemia: insulin should be considered without delay (ADA).

then.value: Multiple Daily Insulin (basal + bolus) and CGM

rules.explanation: T1DM is insulin-dependent; MDI or pump therapy is mandatory (ADA).

then.value: Intensive lifestyle programme: 7% weight loss + 150 min/wk exercise; consider Metformin if BMI >35

rules.explanation: DPP trial: lifestyle reduces conversion to T2DM by 58%.

then.value: Levothyroxine 1.6 µg/kg/day; recheck TSH in 6-8 wk

rules.explanation: Standard replacement dose for primary hypothyroidism.
ADA: screen for prediabetes/T2DM in adults ≥45 yr or BMI ≥25.
Central obesity + HTN + impaired fasting glucose meets several MetS criteria.

then.value: URGENT: very high glucose — rule out DKA / HHS

rules.explanation: Severe hyperglycaemia requires immediate emergency assessment.

then.value: URGENT: HbA1c critically high — initiate insulin & specialist review

rules.explanation: HbA1c ≥12% indicates extreme chronic hyperglycaemia.

then.value: Elderly diabetic — relax HbA1c target to <8% and avoid hypoglycaemia

rules.explanation: ADA Section 13: older adults benefit from individualised, less stringent targets.
Mildly elevated TSH without overt symptoms = subclinical hypothyroidism.

then.value: Weight-loss programme: 5–10% body-weight reduction; refer to dietitian

rules.explanation: 5-10% weight loss markedly improves glycaemic control and cardiovascular risk.
Coexisting diabetes & hypertension multiply CVD risk; start ACEi/ARB.
ADA Section 10: ACEi/ARB + statin reduce CV events in diabetic-hypertensive patients.
Serum uric acid >7 mg/dL is hyperuricaemia.
Diabetics on diuretics/SGLT2-i frequently develop electrolyte disturbances.
